stance_basis: position paper explicitly challenges ORV use on federal lands and calls for phasing out motors from public lands
summary: David Tillotson, President of the Milwaukee Audubon Society, submitted a cover letter and detailed position paper strongly opposing the Draft Environmental Impact Statement on ORV use on public lands. He argues the statement improperly institutionalizes ORV use on federal lands, that the multiple-use concept cannot reconcile wilderness values with ORV use, and that a phased elimination of motorized vehicles from most public lands should begin immediately. He calls for the government to simply say 'NO' to ORV use rather than accommodating it through regulation.
complaint_summary: Tillotson transmits the Milwaukee Audubon Society's position paper opposing ORV use on public lands to the Department of Interior, requesting it reach the proper agency before the hearing.

statement.text:
14 Mar 1973
Mr. Nathaniel Reed US Department of Interior Washington, D.C. 20340
Dear Mr. Reed,
Attached is a position paper of the Milwaukee Audubon Society dealing with the subject of Off The Road Recreational Vehicles on Public Land.
It is our understanding that public reaction was invited to a draft statement on ORV use issued by one of Interior's subagencies - the Eureau of Outdoor Recreation.
We trust that you will see that our position on the ORV matter gets to the proper agency in time for the hearing on this matter.
Sincerely
David Tillotson
President - Milwaukee
Audubon Society
12259 Underwood Fkwy
Wauwatosa, Wis 53226
CC: Cynthia Wilson (Natl Audubon)
CC: Ed Brigham (Natl Midwest Audubon Rep)
